claims.text: OpenAI released a new model called gpt-6-astra.
The gpt-6-astra model is for GPT-6 Astra.

stories.developer_impact: Developers may need to update their integration code or API calls to target the new gpt-6-astra model and consider any changes introduced in the llm 0.35 release.
stories.headline: OpenAI announces GPT-6 Astra model and llm 0.35 release
stories.what_happened: The document reports a release labeled "llm 0.35" and announces a new OpenAI model called "gpt-6-astra" (GPT-6 Astra).
stories.why_it_matters: A new GPT-6 variant could provide improved capabilities for AI applications, and the llm 0.35 release may include updates or features for developers working with large language models.

stories.developer_impact: Developers may gain access to new APIs or frameworks for building multi‑agent systems and agents that retain follow‑up state, reducing the need to implement custom persistence.
stories.headline: OpenAI releases new agent swarm and Lindy Agent with persistent follow‑up capability
stories.what_happened: OpenAI announced another agent swarm and introduced a Lindy Agent designed to never drop a follow‑up.
stories.why_it_matters: The swarm could enable more complex, coordinated AI tasks, while the Lindy Agent’s follow‑up reliability may improve task completion and user experience.

stories.developer_impact: Developers should audit any dependencies on legacy certificates, ensure current TLS configurations use keys of at least 2048 bits, and replace or revoke old certificates that were signed with the compromised keys.
stories.headline: RSA keys of 1990s Certificate Authority factored

sources.title: I've factored the RSA keys of a Certificate Authority from the 90s

stories.what_happened: A researcher announced that they have successfully factored the RSA private keys used by a Certificate Authority that issued certificates in the 1990s, demonstrating that those keys can now be broken with modern computational techniques.
stories.why_it_matters: The break demonstrates that legacy RSA keys of insufficient size are no longer secure, potentially compromising any systems still trusting certificates signed with those keys and highlighting the need to retire or re‑issue old certificates.

stories.headline: OpenAI prioritizes rapid training of smarter models for defensive AI systems
stories.what_happened: OpenAI says its deployment efforts will focus on building powerful, aligned AI to defend against threats from other AI, secure infrastructure, and create new protective measures, emphasizing the need to train smarter models quickly.
stories.why_it_matters: If AI systems become dangerous, having aligned defensive AI could protect critical infrastructure and counter rogue agents in real time, reducing existential risks from advanced AI.
